title: The American Dream: immigration in the 20th century

atoms.b:
European Migration 1892-1954
Ellis Island, opened in 1892, became the main ((entry_point)) for millions of immigrants, mainly from Southern and Eastern Europe. The island played a ((key)) role in building the ((urban)) workforce and transforming American cities in the first half of the 20th century. It was closed in 1954.

atoms.a: Southern and Eastern Europeans mostly worked in agriculture.

feedback.wrong: Southern and Eastern Europeans played a key role in the urban workforce.

atoms.b:
The Impact of World War II
The war lead to labour ((shortages)) in agriculture, so the US established the Bracero Program (1942–1964) which brought millions of Mexican workers into the states. In the ((aftermath)) of the conflict the Displaced Persons Act of 1948 allowed 200,000 Europeans who had been ((uprooted)) by the war to settle permanently in the States. Many among them were Jewish.

atoms.a: The Bracero Program (1942-1962) lead to an unnecessary surplus of labourers.

feedback.wrong: The program helped fill labour shortages in the US.

atoms.a: The Displaced Persons Act 1948 only helped Jewish refugees to settle in the US.

feedback.wrong: The Act helped many but not just Jewish Europeans.

atoms.b:
The Cold War
US intervention, decolonial movements and the socialist bloc shaped ((global)) politics after 1945. This set many migrants in motion to move across the world. The Immigration and Nationality Act of 1965 ended the race and national origin quotas and established a ((preference)) system based on family reunification and skills. This lead to an increase in migration from Latin America and Asia. For example, due to the ((dictatorship)) in Chile, ((refugees)) often fled to the US between 1973-1990.

atoms.a: After changing legislations in the 60s, immigration from Asia and Latin America decreased.

feedback.wrong: Immigration from Asia and Latin America continued to increase.

atoms.a: The Immigration and Nationality Act (1965) ended immigration restriction based on race or nationality.
